argument.notes: S003–S005 correctly give ofReal(s+1)≤dimH Fmax for every 0<s<D. In S006 set q=dimH Fmax and, under L3 only, t=q.toReal. Then t≥0, q=ofReal t and t<D+1. With m=max(0,t-1), D>0 gives 0≤m<D; sstar=(D+m)/2 satisfies 0<sstar<D and t≤m+1<sstar+1. Thus q<ofReal(sstar+1), contradicting F005. Negating L3 gives ofReal(D+1)≤q, and nonnegative-real addition identifies this with dimH E+1≤q. This is an explicit endpoint argument, requiring no limit exchange.

background_notes.fact: For every finite n, Rn(n) is second countable. Its max-metric product with ℝ is second countable, and the Borel sigma algebra of that metric is the product of the two Borel sigma algebras. Rn(n) is realized by finite real tuples, so also has the stated universe-0 realization.

grounds.reason: Rn(n) is finite-dimensional Euclidean space, including the one-point n=0 case, with its Borel structure.
The ambient product is Rn(n)×ℝ with the max metric and Borel structure.
This is the rational-box and rectangle-base justification actually invoked in S001.

background_notes.justification: For n>0, boxes with rational endpoints form a countable base: each point in an open Euclidean ball lies in a sufficiently small such box contained in the ball, using the finite-coordinate norm bound. For n=0 the singleton is a finite base. Rational intervals give a countable base for ℝ; products of base members are a countable base for the max metric. Rectangles of Borel sets are Borel by continuous coordinate projections, while every metric-open set is a countable union of basic open rectangles. These two inclusions prove equality of the Borel and product sigma algebras. Finite tuples of real numbers require no larger universe.

background_notes.fact: For q∈[0,∞], the total real-value map q.toReal takes the finite value of q when q<∞ and takes 0 at ∞. For finite q, t=q.toReal satisfies t≥0 and ofReal t=q. The map ofReal preserves and reflects order on nonnegative reals and preserves their sums. Consequently q<ofReal(D+1), with D≥0 real, implies q<∞, 0≤t<D+1 and q=ofReal t; comparisons with ofReal(sstar+1) can then be made as real comparisons whenever sstar+1≥0.

grounds.reason: ofReal is the nonnegative-real embedding into the usual extended nonnegative reals, with usual order and addition.
N001 supplies the finite nonnegative D and dimH E=ofReal D; L1 implies D>0.
sstar is defined using the total real-value map before the contradiction branch.
L3 bounds q=dimH Fmax by the finite value ofReal(D+1); only within this branch does the proof use the inverse property.

background_notes.justification: The ordered extended nonnegative reals consist of embedded nonnegative reals together with a greatest element ∞. A value below a finite embedded real is finite and therefore has a unique nonnegative real representative, which is its toReal value. Order and addition on finite representatives are the real ones. Thus all stated inverse, comparison and sum identities follow from the embedding; outside the finite case the total convention gives a defined sstar without granting an inverse identity.
